info.album: Rockin' Around The Christmas Tree (Reimagined By Filous)

podcast.body: Recorded and released as a single in 1958 when Brenda Mae Tarplay (Brenda Lee) was 13 years old, the song didn't chart until 1960, reaching number 14 after she became a teen idol. Due to prevailing trends against holiday music charting well, it couldn't crack the Top 10 even at the height of her fame. In the streaming era, it returned to the Hot 100 every Christmas starting in 2013, steadily gaining strength. In 2023, after four years of peaking at number two behind Mariah Carey, and aided by a new music video featuring the 78-year-old Brenda lip syncing to her 13-year-old vocals, it finally topped the Hot 100. This set multiple chart records: the longest climb to number one (65 years), Lee as the oldest chart topper ever (78), and the longest gap between number one hits (63 years). "Brenda Lee's rockin' around the Christmas tree is an inspiring comeback story."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: This song was recorded onto the world's smallest "vinyl" record, which measured only 15 micrometers across. Created by the Nano Made section at the Technical University of Denmark, this tiny record played for 25 seconds in stereo. "Record runs just 25 seconds and what's on it? Brenda Lee's rocking around the Christmas tree."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
